failure_modes: Co-isolated non-vesicular particles mimic intact-EV signature (co-localize with particle peaks, bind capture reagents, and show apparent protection/deprotection behavior) despite absence of bona fide membrane-bound EVs (related evidence: ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Capture-reagent binding to soluble or aggregated proteins (or to lipoproteins) produces marker-positive signal that is insensitive to true membrane-disruption conditions or that is variably sensitive depending on assay conditions, producing inconsistent discrimination between preparations (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Particle enumeration methods (NTA/TRPS) report counts from non-EV particulates (protein aggregates, lipoproteins, salts/precipitates), leading to misleading particle:protein ratios and false co-localization with capture signals (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Detergent, protease, or RNase treatment conditions either (a) fail to fully disrupt some EV subpopulations (false negative for membrane-protection) or (b) denature/aggregate non-vesicular material causing artifactual loss of signal that mimics membrane-protection loss, confounding interpretation.

Source-cell or isolation-process variability (marker absence or low abundance on MSC-EVs, marker shedding, or marker stripping during processing) reduces sensitivity of immuno-capture, causing false negatives and making the attribute non-discriminatory (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi highlights source/scale considerations).

Route- or species-specific delivery or labeling artifacts (as observed in macaque intranasal studies) produce discordant downstream validation in in vivo translational studies despite in vitro analytical discrimination, undermining the utility of the attribute for CMC/potency linkage (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

Assay reproducibility and validation burdens (multiple orthogonal platforms, density gradients, capture reagents) create resource and timeline risks; partial/qualitative readouts lead to ambiguous pass/fail decisions and block downstream CMC actions (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
strongest_objection: The proposed intact-EV signature can be confounded by co-isolated, non-vesicular particulate material (protein aggregates, lipoproteins, or formulation-derived micelles) that (a) co-fractionates with particles, (b) binds canonical ‘‘EV’’ capture reagents or phospholipid-binding reagents, and (c) displays apparent detergent/protease/RNase sensitivity or particle-associated signal changes—producing a false-positive classification of an EV-enriched preparation. This failure is bounded and plausible given MISEV2023 warnings about non-vesicular contaminants and is directly supported by large-animal biodistribution results showing strong nasal retention and low detectable intact EV signal after intranasal dosing (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution), implying that source, formulation, label, or isolation artifacts can dominate readouts and mislead interpretation.
